exemplar.title: What strong work looks like
exemplar.intro: A strong escape-room blueprint proves each clue has exactly one answer — here is how one student built a treasure-hunt clue.

traits.trait: Writes the equation from the story
traits.sample: My clue says: three times the code number plus 7 equals 31 — so the equation is 3x + 7 = 31.
traits.why: The words and the symbols match term by term.

traits.trait: Solves with inverse operations, in order
traits.sample: First I subtracted 7 from both sides to get 3x = 24, then divided both sides by 3 to get x = 8.
traits.why: Each step names the operation AND keeps both sides balanced.

traits.sample: Check: 3(8) + 7 = 31 ✓ — the lock opens, so the clue is fair.
traits.why: Substituting back is the proof a puzzle actually works.

traits.sample: Three of five class trial teams solved my clue, so my observed solve rate was 3 ÷ 5 = 60%.
traits.why: The challenge claim is supported by the student's own labeled test evidence.
